tags.name: Notes
tags.description: iOS-Notes-style Markdown notes with folders, tags, pinning, full-text search, code snippets, attachments, sync and bulk Markdown import/export.

get.description:
Ordered by parent, position and name.

**Scope:** `notes:read`

200.description: All folders of the caller (flat; build the tree from `parent_id`).

post.description:
Creates a folder at the end of its siblings. Names are unique per parent (case-insensitive); nesting is limited to 32 levels and 5000 folders per user.

**Scope:** `notes:write`

409.description: A sibling folder has the same name, or the folder limit is reached.

patch.description:
`parent_id` moves the folder (null = top level; cycles are refused with 409). `position` places it at that index among its siblings (siblings are renumbered 0..n-1); a moved folder without `position` goes last.

**Scope:** `notes:write`

409.description: The move would create a cycle, or a sibling folder has the same name.

delete.description:
Deletes the folder and its subfolders recursively; notes inside are moved to the trash (restorable).

**Scope:** `notes:write`

get.description:
Pinned notes first, then the chosen sort with the note id as tie-breaker; every sort is cursor-paginated (keyset, stable under concurrent edits). `q` searches title, body text (including code) and tags with SQLite FTS5: terms are ANDed, the last term is a prefix, case and diacritics are ignored and FTS operators in the input are treated literally. With `q` and no `sort` the results are ordered by search rank (best first, pinned not hoisted; each user has a separate search index, so ranking and cursors depend only on the caller's own notes); `snippet` then holds the best-matching fragment and `highlights` the matched ranges.

**Scope:** `notes:read`

parameters.name: folder_id
parameters.description: Folder ID (direct children only), or `none` for notes without a folder. Omit for all notes. An unknown folder yields an empty page.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Only notes with this tag (case-insensitive, a leading `#` is ignored).

parameters.name: pinned
parameters.description: Only pinned (true) or unpinned (false) notes. Accepts 1/true/yes/on as true, anything else as false.

parameters.name: trashed
parameters.description: `true` lists the trash instead of live notes.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort key. Default `updated`; with `q` the default is search rank.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Sort order. Default `desc` for `updated`/`created`, `asc` for `title`; ignored for search rank.

post.description:
`body` defaults to an empty note. Tags are normalised (trimmed, lower-cased, leading `#` removed, de-duplicated). `folder_id` must be one of your folders (404 otherwise).

**Scope:** `notes:write`

patch.description:
Partial update. `title: ""` (or null) clears the explicit title so it is derived from the body again; `folder_id: null` moves the note out of its folder. Send `base_version` (the `version` you edited) to avoid overwriting edits from another device: on mismatch the response is 409 with `details.current`. A patch that changes nothing returns the note unchanged (no version bump). Trashed notes can be edited.

**Scope:** `notes:write`

delete.description:
Moves the note to the trash (idempotent). With `permanent=1` the note and its attachments are deleted for good and the id is reported in `deleted_note_ids` of the changes feed.

**Scope:** `notes:write`

parameters.name: permanent
parameters.description: `1` deletes permanently (with attachments) instead of trashing.

post.description:
Restores a trashed note (to "Notes" if its folder no longer exists).

**Scope:** `notes:write`

get.description:
Everything that changed since `since` (omit for a full snapshot), including trashed notes. Pass `server_time` back as `since`: the server clock is strictly monotonic per commit, so no change is ever missed. Deleted ids are kept for 365 days. When `since` predates deletions that have been forgotten since, or is later than the server's clock (for example after a database backup was restored), the response is a full snapshot with `reset: true` (replace local state). Used by the Android and desktop notes apps for offline sync.

**Scope:** `notes:read`

post.description:
Raw body: a `.zip` of `.md`/`.markdown`/`.txt` files (directories become note folders, merged with existing folders of the same name) or a single Markdown/text file (pass `filename`). Front-matter keys `title`, `tags`, `created`, `updated` and `pinned` are honoured. Without a front-matter title the note title is the first heading/line, or the file name when the file does not start with a heading and its first line differs from the name.
Unsafe archive paths (`..`, absolute paths, drive letters) are rejected per entry and reported in `errors`; other file types are reported and skipped; hidden files and `__MACOSX` are ignored. Text is decoded as UTF-8 (BOM/UTF-16 honoured, Latin-1 fallback) with line endings normalised.
Limits: 50 MiB body, 10 000 archive entries, 5 MiB per note, 256 MiB of decompressed Markdown per import; entry sizes are checked before decompression.

**Scope:** `notes:write`

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Name of a single uploaded Markdown file (e.g. `todo.md`); omit for ZIP.

parameters.name: folder_id
parameters.description: Import into this folder (default: top level).

get.description:
ZIP of `.md` files with YAML front matter (`title` when set explicitly, `tags`, `created`, `updated`, `pinned`) laid out in the folder hierarchy; empty folders are included as directory entries. Trashed notes and attachments are not included. File and directory names are made portable (characters invalid on Windows become `_`, duplicates get a ` (2)` suffix). With `folder_id` the archive contains that folder and its subtree under a top-level directory named after it.

**Scope:** `notes:read`

The note as a Markdown file with the same front matter as the ZIP export.

**Scope:** `notes:read`

post.description:
Raw body up to 25 MiB. The MIME type is sniffed from the content (the client Content-Type is ignored); the file name is reduced to its base name. Returns a URL to embed in the note body. Attachments are deleted together with their note.

**Scope:** `notes:write`

get.description:
PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, BMP, AVIF and ICO images are served inline; everything else (including SVG and HTML) as an attachment, with unknown types as `application/octet-stream`. Responses carry a sandboxing CSP and an ETag, and support Range requests.

**Scope:** `notes:read` · also accepts `?access_token=`

note_count.description: Non-trashed notes directly in the folder.

parent_id.description: Move under another folder (`null` = top level). Cycles are rejected.

NotesNoteSummary.description: A note without its body (list views). `title` is the explicit title or the first non-empty line of the body (Markdown removed, at most 200 characters); `snippet` is the following text.

title.description: Explicit title, or the first non-empty line of the body.

snippet.description: Plain-text preview, at most 200 characters (never HTML). With `q` it is the best-matching fragment of the note.

updated_at.description: Last change of title, body or tags (pinning, moving and trashing do not count).

version.description: Incremented on every change (including pin, move, trash, restore); send it back as `base_version` for conflict detection.

has_code.description: The body contains a fenced code block.

body.description: Markdown body (at most 5 MiB; larger bodies are refused with 413). Defaults to "".

title.description: Explicit title; "" or null clears it.

base_version.description: The `version` the client edited. If the note changed since, the update is refused with 409 and `details.current`.

NotesConflictError.description: 409 body for a stale `base_version`: `details.current` is the server copy to merge with.

notes.description: Notes created or changed since `since` (including trashed ones), oldest change first.

folders.description: Folders created, renamed, moved or reordered since `since`.

reset.description: `true` when `since` predates forgotten deletions or lies after the server's clock: the response is a full snapshot and the client must drop notes/folders it does not contain.

file.description: Path inside the archive (or the file name).

url.description: Relative URL to embed in Markdown, e.g. `![](/api/v1/notes/attachments/<id>)`.

NotesHighlights.description: Search matches as `[start, end)` offsets in Unicode code points (not UTF-16 units) into `title` and `snippet`.
